shell.backend-down-body: This can happen the first time you open the app after installing or updating.
shell.backend-down-dev: Start the local services (scripts/dev.sh or scripts/dev.ps1), then reload.

update.installing-body: VideoDubber is downloading this in the background and will restart when it's ready.
update.no-notes: No release notes were published for this version.
update.install-failed: The update could not be installed. You can retry from Settings → Updates.

source-video.title: Download a source video
source-video.subtitle: Fetch a video from Bilibili or Douyin to use as the source for a dubbing project.
source-video.link-hint: A full link, a short link (b23.tv, v.douyin.com), or just the video id all work.
source-video.respect-notice: Only download videos you have the right to use, and please respect the people who made them.
source-video.quality-note: The best available quality varies by video (usually 720p when logged out). Add a session cookie below for sharper sources.

session.heading: Source account (optional)
session.intro: Logged out, most sites only serve lower quality. Paste your own session cookie to download sharper sources. For Bilibili that cookie is SESSDATA and unlocks 1080p (1080p+ and 4K also need a VIP account).
session.warning: Heads up: a session cookie is a live key to your account — anyone holding it can act as you. VideoDubber stores it on this machine as plain text (mode 0600) and sends it only to that site. Remove it here any time, or log out on the site to invalidate it.
session.placeholder: Paste SESSDATA=… or just the value
session.invalid: ✗ Cookie is expired or invalid — downloads are still capped at lower quality. Log in again and paste a fresh one.

source-video.quality-resolved-lower: This video does not offer that — will download at {quality}, the closest available.

home.title: Projects
home.subtitle: Dub a video into another language, fully offline.
home.queue-link: {{ running }} dubbing · limit {{ max }} at a time — change
home.queue-paused: ⏸ The queue is paused — resume it in Settings.
home.empty-body: Create your first dubbing project. Pick a video, choose source and target languages, and let the local pipeline do the rest.

language.heading: Language
language.label: Display language
language.hint: Applies to the whole app immediately, and is remembered next time you open it.

computer.heading: This computer
computer.cloud-suggest: For this machine, cloud processing is suggested for: {{ phases }} — add an API key below, then pick the cloud provider per phase.

defaults.heading: Processing defaults
defaults.intro: The engine used for each phase of new projects. Local engines are private and free; cloud engines can give better quality on weaker hardware but send that phase's data to the service. You can still change providers per project in the wizard, and re-visit this screen anytime.
defaults.render-value: Local FFmpeg — always on this machine (your video never leaves it).
defaults.unavailable: Provider list unavailable — is the local backend running?

keys.heading: Cloud API keys
keys.intro: Optional. Keys are stored only on this machine (~/VideoDubber/credentials.json, owner-only permissions) and are sent only to the service they belong to. Nothing is uploaded anywhere unless you select a cloud provider for a phase.

engines.heading: Engines
engines.intro: Optional high-quality engines for capable machines — accelerated transcription, local LLM translation, neural voices, vocal separation, and forced alignment. They download on demand and run only when a project uses them, so the base app stays small. Packs marked “recommended” suit this computer. Nothing else needs to be installed first.
engines.uv-ok: ✓ Python engines are self-contained{{ bundled }} — just click Install.
engines.uv-download: Python engines (neural voices, separation, alignment) need uv. It isn't bundled in this build, so the first install downloads it automatically (~20 MB, verified) — just click Install.
engines.uv-missing: ⚠ Python engines (neural voices, separation, alignment) need uv, and no build is published for this platform. Install it from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ and reopen.
engines.none: No engine packs are available for this platform, or the backend is offline.
engines.in-use-title: This is the one used for this job
engines.fit-ok: ✓ Your hardware can run this locally
engines.shadowed: Installed, but not in use — “{{ name }}” is better and runs instead.
engines.shadowed-free: You can remove this one to free disk space.
engines.update-title: A newer version is available — reinstall to update
engines.needs-uv-title: This engine needs uv, which has no build for this platform
engines.needs-uv: Needs uv — see the note above.

argos.heading: Translation packs
argos.intro: Offline Argos Translate language packs, downloaded from the Argos index on demand. Non-English pairs translate via English (e.g. Chinese → Vietnamese uses Chinese → English + English → Vietnamese), so install both legs for such a pair. Ollama / cloud translation are not limited to these.
argos.empty: Installed packs appear here. Click “Browse available packs” to see everything you can install.

storage.heading: Storage
storage.intro: Downloaded engine packs, AI models, and caches all live in one app folder. Delete them anytime to free up disk space — VideoDubber re-downloads whatever a project needs on demand. Your projects (the dubbed videos) are never touched.
storage.unavailable: Storage info is unavailable (the backend may be offline).

updates.heading: Updates
updates.browser-note: Update controls are available in the desktop app. You're running in a browser dev session, so checking and installing updates is disabled here.
updates.auto-hint: When on, the app checks for updates on launch and installs them in the background. When off, you update manually below.

about.heading: About VideoDubber
about.body: A local, offline-first video dubbing app. Transcription, translation, and voice synthesis all run on your machine. Only the language models are downloaded on first run.

support.title: Support VideoDubber
support.intro: VideoDubber is free and runs entirely on your machine. If it's useful to you, a donation helps cover development time and keeps it free for everyone. Thank you 🙏
support.bank-hint: Scan the VietQR code with your banking app, or enter the account details manually.
support.qr-alt: VPBank VietQR code for HOANG DUY KHANH, account 184268183
support.bank-name: Vietnam Prosperity Joint Stock Commercial Bank (VPBank)
support.swift-hint: SWIFT/BIC is only needed for international transfers; domestic VietQR transfers use the QR code or the account number above.

export.title: Export
export.no-output: No output yet — render the project to produce a video.
export.preview-unavailable: In-app preview is unavailable here (the browser cannot load local files directly). Use “Open output folder” to play the video.
export.rerender-intro: Produce the final video again with a different subtitle treatment. The dubbed audio is reused; only muxing/burn-in changes.
export.rendering-label: Encoding the final video — this can take a few minutes

processing.title: Processing
processing.stream-offline-title: The live event stream is disconnected
processing.queued-title: ⏳ Waiting to start — #{{ position }} in the queue
processing.queue-capacity: This computer dubs {{ max }} project(s) at a time.
processing.review-body: The transcript is transcribed and translated — no voice has been synthesized yet. Review and adjust the segments (text, per-line fixes, the cast & pronoun sheet), then continue dubbing.
processing.degraded: ⚠ {{ services }} currently unavailable. The run may stall on the affected step until the service is back — services start a few seconds after launch.
processing.waiting-start: Waiting for the pipeline to start…

onboarding.title: Welcome to VideoDubber
onboarding.s1-body: VideoDubber turns a video's spoken audio into another language — transcribe, translate, synthesize a new voice, and remux — all on this machine, fully offline once set up.
onboarding.s1-before: Before your first project we'll quickly:
onboarding.s1-li1: Check this machine has everything it needs to run.
onboarding.s1-li2: Let you pick your source & target languages and a transcription model.
onboarding.s1-li3: Download the AI models for those languages. This needs an internet connection and can take several minutes depending on the model size.
onboarding.s1-hint: The app, media tools and workers are already bundled — only the language models are fetched on first run.
onboarding.s2-warn: Some checks need attention — you can still continue, but downloads or dubbing may fail until they're resolved.
onboarding.s2-unavailable: Couldn't run the checks yet. Make sure the local services have started, then re-check.
onboarding.s3-same-lang: Source and target language must be different.
onboarding.s3-no-pair: No prebuilt translation package is listed for {{ from }} → {{ to }}. The app will try to fetch one, but it may not be available offline.
onboarding.s3-no-catalog: Model catalog unavailable. The default model will be used once services are reachable.
onboarding.s3-voice-download: Download a Piper voice for {{ lang }}
onboarding.s3-voice-hint: A natural offline voice. You can pick a different voice (or add more) later from Settings.
onboarding.s3-no-voice: No bundled Piper voice is listed for {{ lang }} yet. You can add one later from Settings; dubbing will fall back to an available voice.
onboarding.s4-done: ✓ All set — your language models are installed.
onboarding.s4-fetching: Fetching the AI models for {{ from }} → {{ to }} — this one-time download needs an internet connection. Keep this window open.
onboarding.s4-retry-hint: Check your internet connection, then retry — it picks up the remaining models.
onboarding.s4-ready: You're ready to create your first project.

editor.title: Editor
editor.subtitle: Review and refine the translation. Long lines and timing conflicts are flagged below.
editor.preview-unavailable: In-app preview is unavailable here (the browser cannot load local files directly). Use “Open output folder” to play the video.
editor.settings-intro: Review every option applied to this dub. Change an engine, model or voice below, then re-dub from the affected stage — the earlier stages are reused (e.g. a new voice re-renders without redoing transcription or translation).
editor.refine-hint: Review & refine re-reads the whole transcript with a context-capable AI and polishes pronouns/terminology (re-dub from “Review & refine” to apply). Model size (e.g. TranslateGemma 4B → 12B) is managed in Settings → Engines.
editor.redub-title: Re-run the pipeline from “{{ step }}”, reusing the earlier stages
editor.redub-recommended: Your changes take effect from {{ step }} — click that stage to re-dub.
editor.redub-none: No changes yet. You can still re-dub from any stage (e.g. after installing a different model in Settings → Engines).
editor.ctx-intro: Used by context-aware translation (cloud LLMs, Gemma 3 chat, Argos + Gemma repair) to keep pronouns, terms of address, and terminology consistent. Fix something once — e.g. “student → teacher: gọi ‘thầy’, xưng ‘em’” — then Save & re-translate to apply it everywhere.
editor.synopsis-ph: What is this video about, and who is talking to whom?
editor.pronouns-ph: Per speaker pair, the address terms to use (e.g. học sinh → giáo viên: gọi 'thầy', xưng 'em').
editor.save-retranslate-title: Save, then re-run the pipeline from the translation step so the sheet is applied
editor.no-sheet: No translation character sheet yet — one is generated automatically on the first context-aware translation run (cloud LLM, Gemma 3 chat, or Argos + Gemma repair), or create one now to steer pronouns and terminology.
editor.review-hint: No voice has been synthesized yet. Adjust the translations below (and the cast & pronoun sheet), save, then continue — dubbing resumes at speech synthesis.
editor.warnings: ⚠ Some segments have warnings — untranslated lines, over-long subtitles, or timing conflicts.
editor.no-segments: No segments yet. Run the pipeline through the transcription and translation steps first.
editor.untranslated-title: The translation is identical to the source — the translator likely skipped this line. Edit it or re-run translation.
editor.seg-voice-title: Voice used when you regenerate this segment
editor.tighten-title: Re-translate this line shorter so it fits its timing window, then re-synthesize

wizard.title: New project
wizard.keep-hint: Music and effects stay; the original audio is automatically turned down whenever the dubbed voice speaks.
wizard.replace-vocals-hint: Studio-style: the original voices are separated out and replaced by the dub, while the music & effects play at full volume.
wizard.replace-vocals-needs: Install the “Vocal separation” engine in Settings → Engines to enable this.
wizard.remove-hint: Only the dubbed voice is heard. Original speech, music and effects are all muted.
wizard.duck-level: Background volume while the dub speaks
wizard.forced-alignment-hint: Tightens subtitle/dub sync to ~50 ms using the “Forced alignment + diarization” engine.
wizard.fa-not-installed: Not installed — falls back to the default timestamps (install the engine in Settings → Engines for word-accurate timing).
wizard.diarize-hint: Splits the transcript per speaker so multi-speaker videos can use a distinct voice per person. Uses the same engine pack.
wizard.diarize-needs: Install the “Forced alignment + diarization” engine in Settings → Engines to enable this.
wizard.auto-fit: Auto-fit lines that overflow their timing
wizard.auto-fit-hint: When a translated line is too long to fit even at max speed, re-translate it shorter and re-synthesize so it fits — fewer timing conflicts. Works with LLM translators (Ollama / llama.cpp / cloud); ignored for Argos.
wizard.quality-hint: Software H.264 encoding — best size/quality. Only matters when subtitles are burned in.
wizard.fast-hint: Uses the GPU video encoder (VideoToolbox / NVENC) when available — much faster, slightly larger files.
wizard.max-speed-hint: Translated speech is often longer than the original line. The app may speed segments up to this limit to keep them in sync; lines that still don't fit are flagged for review in the editor.
wizard.engines-hint: Each phase can run locally (private, free, works offline) or in the cloud (often better quality on weaker hardware; needs an API key from Settings and sends that phase's data to the service). Defaults come from Settings → Processing defaults.
wizard.refine-hint: A second AI pass re-reads the whole transcript and polishes pronouns, terminology, and flow for consistency. Most useful when Translation runs on Argos or TranslateGemma.
wizard.review-pause: Pause for transcript review before voice synthesis
wizard.review-pause-hint: The pipeline stops once the transcript is translated (and refined) so you can review and hand-adjust the segments in the editor, then continue dubbing when it reads right.
wizard.rendering-hint: Local FFmpeg — always on this machine; your video never leaves it.
wizard.cloud-warn: ☁ Cloud processing enabled for: {{ phases }}. Only that data is uploaded — the video file itself stays local.
wizard.engines-unavailable: Engine list unavailable (backend offline?) — the project will use the local engines.
wizard.voice-omni: Choose a designed voice for OmniVoice. OmniVoice is multilingual, so these work for {{ lang }} (and any language); they ship with the engine pack — if it isn't installed yet, you'll be prompted to install it when the dub starts.
wizard.voice-vieneu: Choose a VieNeu voice for {{ lang }}. These ship with the VieNeu engine pack — if it isn't installed yet, you'll be prompted to install it when the dub starts.
wizard.voice-piper: Choose the Piper voice for {{ lang }}. Any voice not yet on this machine is downloaded automatically when you select it.
wizard.voice-needs-download: This voice isn't installed yet — it downloads automatically when the dub starts (or pick it again to fetch it now).
wizard.voice-omni-fail: Couldn't load the OmniVoice voices — the local services may still be starting. They'll be available once the engine is ready.
wizard.voice-vieneu-vi-only: VieNeu currently provides Vietnamese voices only. For {{ lang }}, pick Piper or a cloud provider in “Processing engines” above.
wizard.voice-piper-none: Piper has no prebuilt voice for {{ lang }} yet — dubbing will fall back to an available voice. To get a natural voice, switch Text to speech to a cloud provider in “Processing engines” above.
wizard.workspace-note: A workspace is created when you continue.
wizard.no-audio-warn: ⚠ This file has no audio stream — there is nothing to transcribe or dub. Pick a different source.
wizard.probe-failed: Media could not be probed automatically. You can still start — the pipeline probes the file as its first step.
wizard.output-folder-ph: (defaults to the project workspace render/ folder)
wizard.output-folder-hint: Final video and any sidecar subtitles are written here.
wizard.preparing-hint: Downloading the AI models for your selected languages — Start unlocks once they're ready (this continues in the background).
wizard.pull-title: Download the local translation model on demand, then start

subtitle-hint.none: Audio dub only, no caption file.
subtitle-hint.srt-file: A separate translated.srt next to the video.
subtitle-hint.vtt-file: A separate translated.vtt (web) next to the video.
subtitle-hint.embedded-soft: Soft subtitle track muxed into the container.
subtitle-hint.burned-in: Rendered permanently into the video pixels.

original-audio.keep: Keep in background (ducked under the dub)

svc.openai-hint: sk-…  — used by cloud STT, translation and TTS

whisper.base: Base — balanced; good on 8 GB (~145 MB)
whisper.large-v3-turbo: Large v3 Turbo — recommended: near-best, 6-8x faster (~1.6 GB)
whisper.distil-large-v3.5: Distil Large v3.5 — English only, fastest large (~760 MB)
whisper.large-v3: Large v3 — best accuracy, slow on CPU (~3 GB)
whisper.phowhisper-medium: PhoWhisper Medium — best for Vietnamese-source audio

confirm.remove-argos-body: Remove the {{ from }} → {{ to }} Argos pack? You can re-install it anytime.
confirm.remove-engine-body: Remove “{{ name }}” and its downloaded files? You can re-install it anytime.
confirm.remove-key-body: Remove the saved {{ service }} API key? Cloud features for this provider stop working until you add a key again.
confirm.clear-storage-body: This removes {{ packs }} engine pack(s) and all downloaded models and caches{{ size }}. Your projects are kept. VideoDubber re-downloads what it needs on demand.

misc.engine-stream-lost: Lost connection to the engine install stream.
misc.engine-stream-lost-fix: The backend connection dropped. Try the install again; if it keeps failing, quit and reopen VideoDubber (in a dev build, restart the local services).
misc.heavy-for-machine: May be heavy for this machine — may run slowly

ducking-hint.strong: Strong (−18 dB) — background well behind the voice
ducking-hint.very-strong: Very strong (−24 dB) — background barely audible

speed-hint.1-3: Gentle speed-up; expect more timing warnings on dense dialogue.
speed-hint.1-6: Good fit for most content; speech stays clearly intelligible.
speed-hint.1-8: Noticeably brisk speech; few timing warnings.
speed-hint.2-0: Minimizes conflicts; speech can sound rushed.

reason.ram-constrained: With {{ ram }} GB RAM, only the smallest local speech-recognition model fits comfortably; cloud STT will be noticeably more accurate.
reason.ram-balanced: {{ ram }} GB RAM runs “large-v3-turbo” — near-best accuracy at 6-8x the speed of large-v3, a great offline balance.
reason.ram-performance: {{ ram }} GB RAM easily runs “large-v3-turbo”; “large-v3” also fits for maximum accuracy if you accept the extra time.
reason.apple-metal: On Apple Silicon, install the whisper.cpp (Metal) engine pack for a large speed-up over the CPU build.
reason.slow-cpu: {{ cores }} CPU cores will make local transcription slow on long videos — consider cloud STT for anything over a few minutes.
reason.nvidia: {{ name }} ({{ vram }} GB) detected — install the CUDA engine packs in Settings → Engines for GPU-accelerated transcription and translation. They need NVIDIA driver 551.61 or newer; on an older driver the app falls back to the Vulkan build automatically.

capacity.one-at-a-time: With {{ cores }} CPU cores and {{ ram }} GB of RAM, one dub at a time keeps this computer responsive — a second would mostly make both slower.
capacity.multiple: {{ cores }} CPU cores and {{ ram }} GB of RAM comfortably cover {{ n }} dubs at once (each one wants about 3 cores and a few GB at its peak).
capacity.cpu-bound: The CPU core count is the limiting factor on this machine.
capacity.ram-bound: Installed memory is the limiting factor on this machine.
capacity.hard-cap: Capped at {{ cap }}: past that, the shared transcription/translation/speech services process work one request at a time anyway.
capacity.heavy-engines: Projects that use a downloadable engine (whisper.cpp, TranslateGemma/Gemma, LibreTranslate, vocal separation, forced alignment) always run one at a time, on any computer — those engines take over the machine and stop each other when they overlap.
capacity.manual: Set manually to {{ n }} simultaneous dub(s) (this computer's recommendation is {{ recommended }}).
